items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I engaged a French pianist whose professional name was Jack Sterling and his real name was Jacques Sansonet... I had been on some gigs at different times with Jack who was quite well known and played nice piano.

ctx.x: I knew of a place on rue Scribe near the American Express Co. so I took him there. When Prez saw that the birds were not live but stuffed and worked with a winding up machine, that gave out the sound of a bird singing, he was very disgusted because he thought the birds were live ones. But he bought perfume and different other things, and when we arrived at the party, it was 7:30! Lily was burning angry with me and she really had reason to be. Some people had been to the cocktail and had to leave early. One was my…

...there was a young trombone player from the British West Indies named Herman Wilson, who had not been very long in Paris and I made his acquaintance with a friend of his named Donald Brown. I was in need of some musicians for my coming jobs in Zurich at the Hungaria -Esquire in June and August in Blankenberge. Donald played bongos and Congo drums, but had never played jazz drums in an orchestra. However, he said that he had a little experience on drums and thought he would catch on to the technique of playing…

The rehearsals went along very well, and Benny made some arrangements to add to those that I had in the books. Everything was cool until the day before we were to leave for Zurich,which was the 30th. A fellow who was also from Martinique came to our hotel and introduced himself, and said that he was a replacement for the bass player. This man's name was Lude. I had seen him around Pigalle, where most of the musicians met, but did not know that he was a bass player until this meeting. Lily and I thought that this…
